articles.desc: Indian equity markets rallied significantly following the results of the US midterm elections, which were favorable for investors. The Nifty Index saw a large gain and reclaimed important moving averages, indicating improved market sentiment. Some consolidation is expected, as the Index approaches broader resistance levels between 25,000 and 25,200. Various sector indices showed differing momentum as they contrasted against the broader Nifty 500 Index.

articles.title: Stubble burning cases cross 3,000 mark in Punjab; Tarn Taran tops list
articles.desc: Punjab has recorded 3,144 incidents of stubble burning between September 15 and November 6, with Tarn Taran as the highest contributor. Fines totaling Rs 54.55 lakh have been imposed in over a thousand cases related to these incidents. Authorities have registered 795 FIRs under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita during this period as well. The practice of stubble burning is often linked to increased air pollution in Delhi-NCR.

articles.title: Dollar jumps after strong US payrolls report
articles.desc: The US dollar index jumped significantly following the Labor Department's report indicating an increase of 165,000 jobs last month, which far exceeded economists' forecasts. As a result, the probability of a rate hike from the Federal Reserve climbed to nearly 80% for next month. Moreover, Federal Reserve officials voiced concerns about ongoing inflation, leading to declines for other currencies such as the euro and sterling against the dollar.

articles.title: Gold drops as strong US payrolls boost dollar, yields
articles.desc: In light of stronger-than-anticipated US payroll figures, gold prices dipped significantly as the data suggested a robust labor market. This development heightened expectations for sustained high-interest rates from the Federal Reserve, bolstering the dollar's strength. Spot gold saw a decline of 0.3% to reach $4,074.36 per ounce, while US gold futures fell by 0.9%. However, Indian retail demand picked up ahead of Diwali festivities, taking advantage of the lower prices.

articles.title: Risk-off mood sweeps European stocks as AI concerns deepen
articles.desc: European markets saw a 1% dip as a wave of selloffs hit insurance stocks following a Democratic victory, raising concerns around the stability of AI investments. A significant downgrade of German reinsurers by JPMorgan added to the insurance sector's woes. Yet, clean energy stocks thrived, bolstered by renewed support for green initiatives.

articles.title: Wall Street stocks rally after heavy AI-related selloff
articles.desc: Wall Street's trading session presented a mixed scenario as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq climbed, contrasting with a modest dip in the Dow. Investor apprehensions regarding impending regulations for the AI sector, especially after recent Democratic electoral successes, led to increased market volatility. Meanwhile, key global markets witnessed declines, particularly in Europe and Asia, overshadowing advancements in certain tech stocks amid a generally bearish sentiment.

articles.title: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
articles.desc: On Friday, technology stocks saw a significant rebound, boosting investor optimism about growth in artificial intelligence amidst recent market fluctuations. The semiconductor sector soared, primarily driven by impressive gains from Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. Although this recovery was strong, the Nasdaq recorded its fourth consecutive weekly fall, hinting at a mixed market outlook. Job indicators remain strong, influencing Federal Reserve interest rate hike expectations.

articles.desc: Amazon said the new text feature lets users research and compare products, track deals and price drops, and have Alexa for Shopping complete purchases on their behalf.

articles.title: USDA to launch AI tool to check crop production data after errors
articles.desc: After the USDA discovered errors in its corn data from September, officials determined the AI tool would have flagged the problem and decided to use it on the crop production report due on November 10, USDA Under Secretary Scott Hutchins said in an interview.

articles.title: Snapchat starts disabling friend-finder feature for UK children, regulator says
articles.desc: Ofcom said the change would make it harder for strangers to contact children on the image-sharing social media platform, one it considers among the largest and most popular online services used by children in Britain.

articles.title: Google acquires Wyoming data center site from AI infrastructure firm Crusoe
articles.desc: Google has acquired Crusoe's data center site in southeast Wyoming, the AI infrastructure developer said on Friday, a day after the Alphabet unit announced a $17-billion investment in the project.

articles.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation: Report
articles.desc: OpenAI completed a substantial funding round, securing $11 billion to increase its valuation to $1.25 trillion. The funding was finalized after the company scaled back its initial plans for over $30 billion. Citing market conditions, OpenAI has encountered shifting investor sentiment toward AI investments and infrastructure costs. Additional funds, which may raise the total to $20 billion, are expected to close soon.

articles.desc: Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA), in a statement on Friday, said the 184 sugar mills have commenced crushing operations across the country as of November 5, 2026, compared to 154 mills during the corresponding period of the preceding year.

articles.title: US stocks today: Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks recover from steep losses, rate fears persist
articles.desc: US stocks rebound as chipmakers recover from Thursday's steep AI-led selloff, lifting the Nasdaq 1.73%. Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Micron lead the recovery, while stronger-than-expected October jobs data revive concerns over a December Fed rate hike. Airbnb rallies after raising its full-year revenue growth forecast, while Atlassian shares decline.

articles.title: NHAI issues guidelines to standardise design and infrastructure for multi-lane free flow tolling
articles.desc: NHAI, in a statement, said the guidelines will ensure that upcoming and ongoing national highway projects are equipped to support MLFF-based barrier-free toll collection without requiring vehicles to stop at toll booths.

articles.title: Vaishnaw puts onus on social media platforms to curb online harm, stops short of safe-harbour clarity
articles.desc: Vaishnaw said social media companies could no longer remain passive intermediaries as the digital ecosystem evolved and must take responsibility for the harmful consequences of content circulated through their platforms, including cyber fraud and so-called digital arrest scams.

articles.title: Want only serious players, no place for frivolous applicants in Semicon 2.0: Vaishnaw to industry
articles.desc: On Friday, the government launched the web application portal for Semicon 2.0, which will initially receive applications related to three of the programme's six pillars: machines and materials, fabs, and packaging. Guidelines have so far been issued only for these three pillars, and the portal is now inviting applications for them. Other three areas pertain to design, R&D and talent.

articles.desc: Hundreds of millions of people worldwide use iPhones, so Apple's choices about which words its keyboard suggests could quietly shape how they communicate. Apple has not publicly disclosed the list, the researcher said.

articles.title: States' capital outlay to accelerate to 10-12% on Centre support in FY27, urban infra to lead: Crisil
articles.desc: States' capital expenditure is projected to rise 10-12% to around Rs 8.5 lakh crore in FY27, driven by higher central assistance and greater fiscal flexibility, according to a Crisil Ratings report. Increased allocation under the SASCI scheme is expected to support infrastructure spending, particularly urban development, roads and bridges.

articles.title: India's 10-year bond posts best week in 7 years, leads emerging Asia as oil slides
articles.desc: This week, Indian government bonds saw a remarkable performance, outpacing other Asian markets as benchmark yields dropped significantly. Following the Democratic win in the US midterms, crude prices fell sharply, enticing foreign investors back to purchase a significant volume of Indian bonds. This shift alleviates pressure on the Reserve Bank of India to maintain elevated yields, contributing to a positive outlook for Indian debt moving forward.
